A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Text2PDE and retain the same core framework and identifiable experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including v2's substantial additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original cylinder-flow and smoke-buoyancy experiments, architecture and conditioning ablations, generated simulations, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds 3D turbulence evaluations, DDIM sampling experiments, autoregressive rollouts, and mesh-radius and flow-regime analyses.

M1.justification: The core mesh autoencoder and latent diffusion architecture remain. Appendices C.3–C.4 add DDIM inference and an autoregressive variant that feeds back the last predicted frame and switches between text and physical-field conditioning by zero-padding the unused modality. These are limited procedural extensions to the retained framework.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates two 2D problems: cylinder flow and buoyancy-driven smoke. V2 retains both and adds 3D turbulent airflow around varied geometric obstacles, extending coverage to a substantially different spatial and physical regime (Section 4.3).

E2.justification: FactFormer is newly evaluated in the 3D turbulence comparison alongside FNO3D and Dil-Resnet (v2 Table 3). The cylinder-flow and smoke-buoyancy comparator sets remain unchanged; the GNN/MGN naming difference in the timing tables does not introduce another baseline.

E3.justification: Headline evaluation changes from L1 to relative L2 error in Tables 1–2. New protocols include relative L2 and log-TKE evaluation for 3D turbulence, DDIM sweeps over 10–100 denoising steps, and cylinder prediction over 100 timesteps in four windows with retrained baselines. The metric replacement alone does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds mesh-radius sensitivity tests, arbitrary-query decoding examples, sampling-step accuracy/speed analysis, longer autoregressive rollout tests, and Reynolds-number/vortex-shedding analysis (B.1, B.3, C.3–C.4, E.1). These investigate component sensitivity, discretization flexibility, efficiency, and temporal stability beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The ten-sample trajectory visualization and timing averages over nine validation samples, or five for PhiFlow, are retained. Additional result rows do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace headline L1 scores with relative L2 scores: cylinder LDM-M-FF changes from 0.0385 L1 to 0.1309 relative L2, not a directly comparable performance change. V2 adds substantial results, including 3D relative L2 errors of 0.602 for LDM-FF versus 0.707 for Dil-Resnet, plus sampling, autoregressive, mesh-radius, and timing results.

T1.justification: The original PDE, kernel, and diffusion formulations remain. V2 adds a cited m^(-1/2) approximation-error scaling statement in B.3 and mathematical claims connecting score Jacobians, potential Hessians, and Langevin mixing in C.3. These extend the theoretical discussion without supplying a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain substantially unchanged. The conclusion now claims that DDIM can make diffusion inference faster than conventional deterministic neural solvers while maintaining accuracy, and reports preliminary autoregressive extensions; v1 presented acceleration and longer-horizon generation as future directions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for DDIM effectiveness, accuracy/computation tradeoffs from kernel radius, 3D smoothing, and penalties from switching conditioning modalities. It explicitly qualifies Reynolds-threshold flow labels as oversimplified. It also removes v1's hypothesis that alternative sampling reduces accuracy by departing from the original objective, materially revising the interpretation of inference alternatives.

D1.justification: Appendices D.3, E.3, and F.3 add the 3D caption template, simulation provenance and viscosity, training hardware, and baseline/LDM hyperparameters, including latent dimensions and patch sizes. C.3–C.4 document sampling and conditioning procedures. This substantially extends reproducibility information; the existing 2D settings and code/data/model release information remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting references on flow-regime classification, vortex shedding, diffusion mixing, and rendering, including Blevins, Bovier, Chen, Gabbai–Benaroya, Zdravkovich, and Koehler. Several numerical-method and fast-sampling references are removed. The central positioning relative to video diffusion and neural PDE solvers remains.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the accessibility motivation and condenses background, conditioning, and related-work explanations, while updating solver terminology, affiliations, and conference status. The six main sections and overall narrative remain recognizable; appendix additions receive new subsections rather than a wholesale document reorganization.

P2.justification: V2 expands Figure 1 with 3D output and adds turbulence visualizations, kernel/query diagrams, DDIM plots, an autoregressive framework diagram, and a Reynolds-number histogram. It also regroups existing autoencoder ablation tables and expands the inference-time display to three benchmarks. These substantially extend and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for applicability and practical use: 3D turbulence extends validation beyond two 2D problems, while DDIM and autoregressive experiments test remedies that v1 only proposed for slow inference and fixed horizons. Added sensitivity analyses, implementation details, and captioning qualifications improve assessability. The strongest speed claims remain limited by inconsistent hardware attribution between Appendix C.3 and Appendix G, and neither version reports training uncertainty, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support.
